title: Design canary rollouts and A/B experiment flows for pinned model version upgrades
creator: Elena Alvarez
description:
Background: When customers pin a model version for production stability, they still need a safe path to upgrade to new versions (patches, quantization changes, or model variants). We must enable canary rollouts and controlled A/B experiments for pinned versions so teams can validate latency, cost, and quality before a global switch.

Goal: Define the end-to-end product flow and acceptance gating for 'pinned model canaries' and A/B tests: how traffic is split, how stickiness is preserved for keys/users, what perf/quality metrics are published as the model's performance profile, and what automation (ramp/rollback) is available to customers and Redwood operators.

Key requirements:
- Traffic routing: support percent-based and cohort-based traffic splits behind pins (e.g., 1%, 10%, 50%), with deterministic assignment by API key or user_id to ensure sticky exposures.
- Canary lifecycle: create canary builds tied to a pinned target (pin -> new_candidate). Candidate receives only the configured percentage until promoted or rolled back.
- A/B experiments: support metric-driven experiments comparing baseline (pinned) vs candidate with pre-defined success metrics. Experiment config must be exportable and reproducible.
- Performance profile publishing: during a canary, collect and publish a provisional performance profile for the candidate; only mark as 'verified' after meeting quality gates. Profiles include latency distributions, token cost delta, memory/KV cache hit rates, and eval-quality metrics on conserved prompt sets.
- Gating and automation: define automated gating rules (latency p95 threshold relative to baseline, error rate ceiling, quality regression limits). If breaches occur, auto-fail and rollback; if gates pass for X hours/requests, auto-ramp according to schedule.
- Visibility & controls: Console UI to create/manage canaries, visual comparison of metrics, one-click promote/rollback, manual pause, and audit logs for promotions. API for infra/automation to control rollouts programmatically.
- Observability hooks: linkable dashboards, per-route token-level cost breakdown, and sample traffic capture for failed cases.
- Private/Dedicated compatibility: same semantics must work for hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments; any automation must respect private control-plane constraints.

Success metrics:
- 95th percentile latency regression <= 10% compared to pinned baseline across candidate for at least 24h and 100k tokens.
- Quality regression (eval set) <= 3% relative to baseline (or configurable per project).
- No increase in model error rate or inference failures > 0.5% absolute.
- Deployment time from canary creation to promoted (or rolled back) captured in audit logs and under SLA for managed promotions.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Product spec for canary and A/B flows with UI mockups and API contract published to Confluence and referenced in this ticket.
2) Deterministic hashing algorithm described and approved for sticky assignments.
3) Standard gating policy defined (defaults + per-customer overrides), including automatic rollback thresholds.
4) Performance profile schema extended to tag provisional profiles during canaries and a 'verified' state post-gate.
5) Console mockups reviewed by Design and Engineering (see comments).
6) End-to-end test plan and required telemetry (metrics/traces/logs) listed and handed to ENG telemetry team.
7) Rollout runbook and operator playbook for emergency rollback present in repo.

Rollout plan (proposal):
- Phase 0 (spec & UI): finalize spec, hashing, gating defaults, and Console mockups (2 weeks).
- Phase 1 (infra): build traffic split/routing primitives, sticky assignment, provisional profile publishing API, and telemetry hooks (3 sprints).
- Phase 2 (console + API): expose canary controls, visibility, promote/rollback buttons, A/B experiment UI and REST API endpoints (2 sprints).
- Phase 3 (pilot): internal + 2 customers pilot for low-volume upgrades, collect feedback, and tighten gates (4 weeks).
- Phase 4 (GA): enable self-serve rollouts; update docs, SDKs, and quickstarts.

Monitoring & experiment analysis:
- Define automated experiment summary that computes deltas and statistical significance for quality metrics.
- Dashboard to compare baseline vs candidate across: p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost per 1k tokens, error rate, eval-set pass rate, KV cache hit ratio, and mem usage.
- Alerts: immediate paging for SLO breaches and an aggregated weekly report for long-running experiments.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: noisy signal on small canaries leads to incorrect promotion. Mitigation: require minimum sample size + statistical test; default min requests = 50k tokens or 24h.
- Risk: stickiness mismatch across multi-route apps. Mitigation: offer per-route assignment and stable hashing on composite key (customer_id + route).
- Risk: Private deployments cannot auto-promote due to control-plane restrictions. Mitigation: provide manual promote API + documented operator steps for Private.

Dependencies: ENG-2891 (canary routing primitives), ENG-3045 (telemetry and perf-profile ingestion), ENG-3210 (pinning API changes), ENG-3300 (Console rollout UI).

Deliverables:
- Confluence spec + API contract link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/ModelOnboard/pm-4217 (placeholder)
- Console mockups: Drive link (placeholder)
- Runbook: repo link (placeholder)

Notes: This ticket should drive cross-functional kickoff with infra, telemetry, design, applied-ml (for eval sets), and solutions engineering for pilot customers. Consider a small feature flag for internal staff to test auto-ramp behavior before wider release.
